title: Filtered colimits of strictly henselian local rings along local maps
statement: Let $I$ be a nonempty small directed poset and $(R_i,\varphi_{ij})_{i\leq j}$ a direct system of commutative local rings, with maximal ideals $\mathfrak m_i$. Assume every $R_i$ is strictly henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] and every transition homomorphism is local, meaning $\varphi_{ij}^{-1}(\mathfrak m_j)=\mathfrak m_i$. Let $R=\varinjlim_iR_i$ be the colimit in commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Then $R$ is a strictly henselian local ring. Neither injectivity nor surjectivity of the transition maps is assumed.

source.place: Tag 04GI, lemma-colimit-henselian, strictly henselian case; statement and proof.

proof.text: Write $\alpha_i:R_i\to R$ for the colimit maps and set $M=\bigcup_i\alpha_i(\mathfrak m_i)$. This is an ideal: move any two representatives, and a representative of any multiplier, to one common stage, and use the ideal axioms there. By [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise], equality of two representatives is witnessed at a common later stage. Thus, if $\alpha_i(x)=\alpha_j(y)$ with $y\in\mathfrak m_j$, some $k\ge i,j$ satisfies $\varphi_{ik}(x)=\varphi_{jk}(y)\in\mathfrak m_k$, and locality gives $x\in\mathfrak m_i$. Consequently $\alpha_i^{-1}(M)=\mathfrak m_i$. In particular $1\notin M$: choose any $i$ (the index is nonempty), and apply this equality to $1\in R_i$.

source.place: Tag 04GI, lemma-colimit-henselian, omitted locality argument: the maximal-ideal union and its contraction, expanded using representatives.

proof.text: Every $r\notin M$ has a representative $r=\alpha_i(x)$ by [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise]; necessarily $x\notin\mathfrak m_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-ring-unit-criterion], choose $y\in R_i$ with $xy=1$, so $\alpha_i(y)$ inverts $r$. Therefore every nonzero element of $R/M$ is invertible, and $M$ is maximal. Every proper ideal of $R$ is contained in $M$, since an element outside $M$ is a unit. Thus $R$ is local with unique maximal ideal $M$, and the contraction equality in step 1 says that every $\alpha_i$ is local.

source.place: Tag 04GI, lemma-colimit-henselian, omitted locality argument; unit criterion Tag 00E9, lemma-characterize-local-ring.

proof.text: Put $\kappa_i=R_i/\mathfrak m_i$ and $\kappa=R/M$. The local transition maps induce compatible field maps $\kappa_i\to\kappa_j$, and $\rho_i([x])=[\alpha_i(x)]$ defines a compatible map $\kappa_i\to\kappa$. Each $\rho_i$ is injective: $\rho_i([x])=0$ means $\alpha_i(x)\in M$, hence $x\in\mathfrak m_i$ by step 1. To verify the colimit universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], take any compatible ring maps $b_i:\kappa_i\to S$. Their composites with $R_i\to\kappa_i$ give a cocone on the $R_i$, hence a unique $b:R\to S$. It kills $M$, because $b(\alpha_i(x))=b_i([x])=0$ for $x\in\mathfrak m_i$, so it factors uniquely through $\kappa$. Conversely any map from $\kappa$ with the required composites must induce that same $b$ after the surjection $R\to\kappa$. This proves $\kappa=\varinjlim_i\kappa_i$ in commutative rings, with the stated $\rho_i$.

source.place: Tag 04GI, lemma-colimit-henselian, omitted residue-field colimit argument, written out by the quotient and colimit universal properties.

proof.text: Let $p\in\kappa[T]$ be nonconstant and separable. By [def-pc-separable-polynomial], choose $U,V\in\kappa[T]$ with $Up+Vp'=1$. Apply [lemma-nagata-filtered-colimit-finite-data] to the directed colimit of step 3: descend the finitely many coefficients of $p,U,V$ and the finitely many coefficient equations of this identity to one $\kappa_i$. Taking zero coefficients outside their chosen finite degree bounds gives polynomials $p_i,U_i,V_i$ with $U_ip_i+V_ip_i'=1$, since differentiation has coefficients $n c_n$ and hence commutes with the coefficient maps. A nonzero positive-degree coefficient of $p$ has a nonzero lift, so $p_i$ is nonconstant; the displayed identity makes it separable. The residue field $\kappa_i$ is separably closed by strict henselianity [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. By [def-pc-separably-closed], choose $c_i\in\kappa_i$ with $p_i(c_i)=0$. Applying $\rho_i$ gives $p(\rho_i(c_i))=0$. Thus $\kappa$ is separably closed by the same definition.

source.place: Tag 04GI, lemma-colimit-henselian: the separably closed residue-field sentence, expanded by descending a Bezout identity.

proof.text: Now let $f\in R[T]$ be monic of degree $n$, and let $a_0\in\kappa$ satisfy $\overline f(a_0)=0$ and $\overline{f'}(a_0)\ne0$. Use [lemma-nagata-filtered-colimit-finite-data] for $R$ to lift the finitely many coefficients below degree $n$ to some stage; form the lift with leading term exactly $T^n$. By [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise] for the colimit of step 3, lift $a_0$ to some $a_{0,j}\in\kappa_j$. Move both choices to a common upper bound $i$. This gives a monic $f_i\in R_i[T]$ mapping to $f$ and $a_{0,i}\in\kappa_i$ with $\rho_i(a_{0,i})=a_0$.

source.place: Tag 04GI, lemma-colimit-henselian: choose a monic polynomial and its residue root at one sufficiently large index.

proof.text: The coefficient formulas for evaluation and differentiation, and $\rho_i([x])=[\alpha_i(x)]$, give $\rho_i(\overline{f_i}(a_{0,i}))=\overline f(a_0)=0$ and $\rho_i(\overline{f_i'}(a_{0,i}))=\overline{f'}(a_0)\ne0$. Injectivity of $\rho_i$ from step 3 gives $\overline{f_i}(a_{0,i})=0$; the second equality gives $\overline{f_i'}(a_{0,i})\ne0$. The ring $R_i$ is henselian by [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], so implication (i)$\Rightarrow$(ii) of [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-local-root-lifting] supplies $a_i\in R_i$ with $f_i(a_i)=0$ and $[a_i]=a_{0,i}$. For $a=\alpha_i(a_i)$, applying the ring map to the finite evaluation sum gives $f(a)=\alpha_i(f_i(a_i))=0$, and reduction gives $[a]=\rho_i([a_i])=a_0$.

source.place: Tag 04GI, lemma-colimit-henselian, final simple-root lifting argument; the criterion in the idempotent convention is Tags 04GF/04GG and 09XI.

proof.text: We have proved the monic simple-root lifting condition for the local ring $R$. Implication (ii)$\Rightarrow$(i) of [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-local-root-lifting] makes $R$ henselian in the idempotent-lifting convention. Its residue field is separably closed by step 4. Therefore $R$ is strictly henselian by [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology].
